newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit slips on trade deficit, but fall limited.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit slips on trade deficit, but fall limited.

text.p: * Ringgit falls back after large June trade deficit
* Dollar/ringgit rise capped by talk of profit-taking above 2.6400
* Ringgit seen rangebound in Asian trading
The ringgit fell back against the dollar on fresh selling after the release of a larger than expected Malaysia's trade deficit for June, dealers said.

"Ringgit selling started in London last night after the release of the trade figures and continued in Sydney this morning," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "But some Kuala Lumpur names were seen selling dollar/ringgit at the 2.6370 level."
Dollar gains were also capped by talk of profit-taking above 2.6400, he said.
Malaysia on Monday reported a trade deficit of 2.8 billion ringgit for June against a surplus of 156.2 million in May.

At 0145 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6300/30 to a dollar. It closed at 2.6090/120 in Kuala Lumpur on Monday after hitting a high of 2.5800 following Bank Negara's announcement of curbs on currency swaps by Malaysian banks.
Bank Negara said on Sunday that local banks will have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday.
The curbs are part of an effort to cool speculation in the ringgit which has been under attack from currency speculators over the past month.

Dealers said they expected the ringgit to be rangebound during Asian trading. But they added that given the flushed liquidity in the offshore market, the dollar has scope to retest its recent high of 2.6530 against the ringgit.
